tldr: REALTALK is a 21-day real-world dataset of authentic messaging app dialogues between human participants, used to benchmark LLM performance on persona simulation and long-term memory recall, revealing that models struggle with both tasks compared to human conversational patterns.
contributions: Introduction of REALTALK, a 21-day corpus of 10 authentic human-human messaging conversations totaling over 17,000 tokens per conversation
Dataset analysis comparing emotional intelligence (EI) attributes and persona consistency between real-world human dialogues and LLM-simulated conversations
Two benchmark tasks: persona simulation (continuing a conversation on behalf of a specific user) and memory probing (answering questions requiring long-term recall)
728 human-annotated memory probing QA pairs categorized into multi-hop, temporal reasoning, and commonsense types
methods: Ten US participants aged 18-25 were paired to engage in daily messaging conversations over 21 days, producing 10 unique conversations with ~21.9 sessions each. A separate group of annotators created 728 memory-probing QA pairs (302 multi-hop, 321 temporal reasoning, 111 commonsense) and documented speaker events per session. EI was evaluated at both message and speaker levels using metrics including reflectiveness, grounding acts, emotion/sentiment diversity and stability, intimacy progression, and empathy scores derived from LLM-based and fine-tuned RoBERTa classifiers.
results: Human dialogues exhibit greater emotion and sentiment diversity, gradually build intimacy over time, and show high variance in EI attributes, while LLM-simulated conversations (LOCOMO) display excessive empathy, predominantly positive tone, and more uniform EI. LLMs struggle to simulate a user solely from dialogue history, but fine-tuning on specific user chat history improves persona emulation. Existing models face significant challenges in recalling and leveraging long-term context, as demonstrated by poor performance on memory probing questions.
limitations: The dataset consists of only 10 participants, all native speakers from the US aged 18-25, limiting demographic diversity. The paper notes that real-world human dialogues are inherently noisy (typos, abbreviations, slang), which may pose additional challenges for model evaluation. No explicit limitations section is provided beyond these inherent constraints of a small, demographically narrow dataset.
